lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1733 — reinforcement: raise the ceiling, keep the damage

Option B, built on the two prerequisites shipped in OTA-1732.

⚠⚠⚠ THE LADDER IS FLAT, FROM THE CATALOG. Each level adds 20% of the weapon's
CATALOG BASE to that copy's temper-rolled maximum. On a base-50 weapon the step is
a flat 10, and your three copies come out exactly as specified:

    catalog base 50 → step 10
      temper 20:  20 → 30 → 40 → 50
      temper 50:  50 → 60 → 70 → 80
      temper 90:  90 → 100 → 110 → 120

A percentage of the INSTANCE max would have paid a lucky roll three times over
(90 → 108 → 130 → 156). That is the thing your ruling rules out, and the suite
holds the flat step against exactly those three copies.

⚠⚠ NO SECOND DURABILITY AUTHORITY. `baseMax` and `reinforced` live on
`item.durability` — the object repair, wear and the item card already own. `max`
keeps its meaning; nothing else learns a new field. The catalog is READ once, for
the size of the step, and never written: a second copy of the same weapon still
mints at its own temper roll, and the suite asserts the row itself never moved.

⚠ `baseMax` NEVER MOVES. It is stamped at mint as the temper roll and is not
rewritten by a reinforcement, so `max` is recomputed as `baseMax + step × level`
rather than accumulated — the ladder is a pure function of two stored numbers and
cannot compound or drift on rounding.

⚠ THE LEVEL CANNOT BE DERIVED, which is why it is stored. Temper already
randomises the ceiling, so 60 on a base-50 sword is either an unreinforced lucky
roll or a reinforced average one and the number alone cannot tell you which.

⚠⚠ OTA-1654's RULE, REUSED: raising a ceiling CARRIES the damage rather than
repairing it. 7/23 reinforced by 10 is 17/33 — still 16 points down.

⚠ AND A MEASUREMENT CORRECTED ME THERE. I asserted the mend would then cost MORE.
It does not, and that is the rule being exactly right: the same points are missing,
so `repairCost = missing × rarity` is the same number. What changed is where a full
mend REACHES. Paying to strengthen a weapon must not quietly inflate the price of
mending it, and it does not.

COSTS, both escalating, both built on ladders that already existed:

    TC        140 → 300 → 640, through REPAIR_RARITY_MULT — the SAME rarity
              opinion repair uses, hoisted so one table serves both rather than
              the game holding two views of what a Legendary is worth.
    materials (level+1) × the full-repair bill, via reinforceCostMaterials built
              on repairCostMaterials — the escalation expressed in the stock the
              item is already made of, not a new table.

    measured: TC 420 → 900 → 1920 · material units 16 → 32 → 48 (Rare, base 50)

⚠ BOTH ARE CHECKED BEFORE EITHER IS SPENT — OTA-984's lesson at this same counter.
Short of coin or short of parts, nothing moves and the refusal names what is
missing.

SHAPES THAT ARE NOT A PLAIN CATALOG WEAPON:
  · FUSED / generated — no catalog row to take 20% of (lookupBaseDurability misses
    by design, OTA-705), so its own temper roll is its base. 30/40 → 38/48.
  · LEGACY saves with neither field read as `baseMax = max, reinforced = 0` — the
    truth for a weapon nobody has reinforced. 18/37 reinforces cleanly with NO
    migration and no backfill pass.

16 tests covering every case you listed: levels 0→1→2→3, the fourth refused (and
charging nothing), low/average/high temper copies, a damaged weapon, repair after
reinforcement, a fused weapon, a generated weapon, a legacy weapon, save/reload at
EACH level, insufficient TC, insufficient materials, no smith present, and
sell → buy back and sell → reload → buy back both keeping the reinforcement.

19 gates green. Complete surface: 1212 suites, 12508 tests, 0 failures.
